docs.title: Dedicated to my students
docs.text:
These resources have been selected to provoke curiosity and exploration, provide useful knowledge, and expose you to different ideas and perspectives. Inclusion does not mean that every claim or argument in a book is endorsed. Books are different kinds of sources: scientific research, popular science, journalism, history, memoir, criticism, practical guides, and works of argument. Read accordingly. Ask what evidence supports a claim, what perspective the author brings, what may have changed since publication, and what credible alternative interpretations exist.

Remember: you can take a stand while remaining open to changing your mind as you learn more. Science advances by revising what we think we know. So can you.

docs.title: Explore
docs.text:
These resources have been selected as starting points for exploration. You are not expected to read or watch everything. Follow your interests, compare different sources and question what you encounter.

Readings - Fiction - Non-fiction

Glossary - Think like you care module

This collection will continue to grow along with our community.

docs.title: Contributions
docs.text: Students and collaborators are welcome to suggest additions. Before recommending a resource, please consider: * Is it accurate and trustworthy? * Is it appropriate for students? * Have you read or reviewed it? * Is the link legal and reliable? * Does it add something useful to the collection?

docs.title: Start here!
docs.text: Before exploring the collection, take a moment to read the About to understand what this project is about and how to make the most of it.

docs.title: Fiction
docs.text: Reading selection to encourage curiosity, imagination, empathy, critical thinking, and exploration of different perspectives, cultures, and possible worlds. (order: author's surname)

docs.title: Things Fall Apart — Chinua Achebe
docs.text: A novel about Igbo society and the disruptive arrival of British colonial rule and Christian missionaries in what is now Nigeria. #colonialism #nigeria #culture #identity #history #african-literature #classic

docs.title: Americanah — Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
docs.text: A novel about migration, race, identity, relationships, and belonging, viewed through the experiences of a Nigerian woman living between Nigeria and the United States. #migration #race #identity #belonging #nigeria #society

docs.title: Fahrenheit 451 — Ray Bradbury
docs.text: A novel about censorship, conformity, mass media, and a society increasingly disconnected from books, reflection, and independent thought. #dystopia #censorship #media-literacy #conformity #critical-thinking #classic

docs.title: Kindred — Octavia E. Butler
docs.text: A contemporary Black woman is repeatedly transported to a slave plantation in nineteenth-century Maryland, confronting the relationship between history, race, power, family, and survival. #historical-fiction #race #slavery #history #power #identity #recommended

docs.title: Lilith's Brood (Xenogenesis Trilogy) — Octavia E. Butler
docs.text: Dawn · Adulthood Rites · Imago After humanity nearly destroys itself, the surviving humans encounter the Oankali, an alien species offering survival at a profound biological and social cost. Across three novels, Butler explores consent, power, difference, race, gender, hierarchy, genetic engineering, and what it means to remain human while becoming something new. #science-fiction #bioethics #genetics #consent #power #identity #race #gender #humanity #recommended

docs.title: Parable of the Sower — Octavia E. Butler
docs.text: A young woman navigates a collapsing society shaped by inequality, violence, and environmental crisis while trying to imagine a different future. #speculative-fiction #climate #inequality #community #resilience #society

docs.title: The Three-Body Problem — Liu Cixin
docs.text: A science-fiction novel connecting fundamental physics, China's Cultural Revolution, technological development, and humanity's response to the possibility of extraterrestrial intelligence. #science-fiction #physics #technology #china #history #first-contact

docs.title: The Neverending Story — Michael Ende
docs.text: A fantasy novel about a boy who enters the world of a mysterious book, exploring imagination, storytelling, identity, desire, and the relationship between the worlds we create and the lives we live. #fantasy #imagination #storytelling #creativity #identity #coming-of-age #german-literature #recommended

docs.title: Cien años de soledad (Cem Anos de Solidão) — Gabriel García Márquez
docs.text: A multigenerational story of the Buendía family and the fictional town of Macondo, blending history, myth, politics, memory, and the extraordinary to explore recurring patterns in families and societies. #magical-realism #family #memory #history #latin-america #colombia #society #classic #recommended

docs.title: Lessons in Chemistry — Bonnie Garmus
docs.text: A novel centred on a female chemist confronting sexism and restrictive social expectations in the 1950s and 1960s, combining science, humour, and questions about equality and opportunity. #science #chemistry #gender-equality #women-in-science #discrimination #society

docs.title: A Árvore das Palavras — Teolinda Gersão
docs.text: A coming-of-age novel set in colonial Mozambique, exploring childhood, family, race, colonialism, belonging, and the tensions between different cultural worlds. #colonialism #mozambique #race #identity #belonging #history #portuguese-literature

docs.title: A Cidade de Ulisses — Teolinda Gersão
docs.text: A novel in which Lisbon becomes both setting and subject, intertwining memory, love, art, identity, and the ways people construct stories about places and about themselves. #identity #memory #art #place #lisbon #relationships #portuguese-literature

docs.title: Os Teclados — Teolinda Gersão
docs.text: A novel about a young girl's encounter with music, family expectations, artistic vocation, and the struggle to create an independent inner life. #music #creativity #identity #family #women #art #portuguese-literature

docs.title: Homegoing — Yaa Gyasi
docs.text: An intergenerational novel following two branches of a Ghanaian family across centuries, connecting slavery, colonialism, migration, racism, memory, and inherited history. #historical-fiction #ghana #slavery #colonialism #race #family #memory

docs.title: The Midnight Library — Matt Haig
docs.text: A novel about regret, possibility, alternative lives, and the choices through which people construct meaning and value. #contemporary-fiction #choices #identity #meaning #perspective

docs.title: Brave New World — Aldous Huxley
docs.text: A dystopian exploration of technological control, consumerism, conformity, pleasure, and the tension between individual freedom and social stability. #dystopia #technology #society #conformity #ethics #classic

docs.title: Never Let Me Go — Kazuo Ishiguro
docs.text: A quiet and unsettling novel that raises questions about humanity, biotechnology, mortality, social acceptance, and the ethical boundaries of scientific progress. #speculative-fiction #bioethics #technology #humanity #identity #ethics #recommended

docs.title: Flowers for Algernon — Daniel Keyes
docs.text: A moving exploration of intelligence, disability, scientific experimentation, dignity, relationships, and what we mean when we call someone intelligent. #science-fiction #intelligence #disability #ethics #science #empathy #recommended

docs.title: The Left Hand of Darkness — Ursula K. Le Guin
docs.text: A landmark science-fiction novel that uses an unfamiliar society to explore gender, identity, culture, politics, and what it means to understand people different from ourselves. #science-fiction #gender #identity #culture #society #recommended

docs.title: A Wrinkle in Time — Madeleine L'Engle
docs.text: A young science-fiction adventure across space and time that combines mathematics, individuality, courage, family, and resistance to conformity. #science-fiction #mathematics #space #individuality #family #curiosity #classic

docs.title: The Memory Police — Yoko Ogawa
docs.text: A surreal novel about an island where objects, memories, and eventually parts of people's lives systematically disappear, exploring memory, loss, authoritarianism, and resistance. #speculative-fiction #memory #authoritarianism #identity #loss #resistance

docs.title: 1984 — George Orwell
docs.text: A dystopian novel about totalitarianism, surveillance, propaganda, language, and the manipulation of truth. #dystopia #surveillance #propaganda #language #power #critical-thinking #classic

docs.title: Animal Farm — George Orwell
docs.text: A political allegory about a group of farm animals whose rebellion against their human owner develops into a new system of oppression, exploring power, propaganda, inequality, and the corruption of revolutionary ideals. #allegory #power #propaganda #inequality #authoritarianism #politics #critical-thinking #classic #recommended

docs.title: Frankenstein — Mary Shelley
docs.text: A foundational work of science fiction exploring scientific ambition, responsibility, creation, isolation, and the consequences of rejecting what we do not understand. #science-fiction #science #ethics #responsibility #identity #classic #recommended

docs.title: Cat's Cradle — Kurt Vonnegut
docs.text: A satirical novel about science, technological responsibility, belief, and the unintended consequences of human invention. #science #technology #ethics #responsibility #satire #society #recommended

docs.title: Slaughterhouse-Five — Kurt Vonnegut
docs.text: A darkly comic and fragmented anti-war novel about memory, trauma, fatalism, and the absurdity of trying to make sense of mass destruction. #war #memory #trauma #absurdism #society #critical-thinking #recommended

docs.title: The Martian — Andy Weir
docs.text: A survival story built around engineering, scientific reasoning, improvisation, and solving one problem after another under extreme constraints. #science-fiction #engineering #problem-solving #space #science #resilience #recommended

docs.title: Project Hail Mary — Andy Weir
docs.text: A science-fiction adventure centred on scientific discovery, experimentation, problem-solving, communication, and cooperation in the face of an existential challenge. #science-fiction #science #problem-solving #space #communication #cooperation

docs.title: Non-fiction
docs.text: An evolving collection, with selected chapters or extracts connected to activities. The groupings indicate a starting point; several books are relevant across disciplines. Some titles are available to read legally online at no cost. These are marked 🆓

docs.title: How Life Works — Philip Ball
docs.text:
An exploration of contemporary biology that challenges simplified explanations of genes, organisms, and biological systems.

#biology #science #systems-thinking #genetics #complexity

docs.title: Surely you’re joking Mr Feynman - Ralph Leighton, Richard Feynman 🆓
docs.text:
A collection of humorous and insightful autobiographical stories from Nobel Prize-winning physicist Richard Feynman. celebrating curiosity, independent thinking, and the joy of learning.

#scientific-method #critical-thinking #problem-solving #curiosity #physics #recommended

docs.title: Bad Science — Ben Goldacre 🆓
docs.text:
An accessible examination of scientific evidence, misleading claims, statistics and the way science is communicated in the media. Learn how to evaluate scientific claims, understand statistics, and recognise common mistakes in science communication.

#critical-thinking #scientific-literacy #statistics #recommended

docs.title: The Demon-Haunted World. Science as a Candle in the Dark — Carl Sagan 🆓
docs.text:
An exploration of scientific thinking, skepticism, and the importance of evidence in distinguishing reliable knowledge from pseudoscience, superstition, and misinformation. Sagan argues for science not only as a body of knowledge, but as a way of questioning claims, recognising uncertainty, and thinking critically about the world.

#scientific-literacy #critical-thinking #scientific-method #pseudoscience #misinformation #recommended

docs.title: Thinking, Fast and Slow — Daniel Kahneman
docs.text:
An influential exploration of judgment and decision making, contrasting fast, intuitive responses with slower, more deliberate reasoning and examining the biases that can affect both. Note: some studies discussed in the book, particularly research on social priming, were later challenged during psychology's replication crisis. A useful opportunity to explore how scientific knowledge changes. See Kahneman's 2012 open letter on social priming.

#psychology #decision-making #cognitive-bias #reasoning #behaviour #critical-thinking

docs.title: Not Born Yesterday — Hugo Mercier
docs.text:
An exploration of why humans are not as gullible as commonly assumed, examining how we evaluate information, trust others, and decide what to believe.

#critical-thinking #psychology #trust #misinformation #reasoning #communication

docs.title: Free Agents — Kevin J. Mitchell
docs.text:
An exploration of agency and free will through neuroscience, evolution, and biology, arguing that living organisms have evolved increasingly sophisticated capacities to make choices and act on their own reasons.

#neuroscience #biology #free-will #agency #decision-making #behaviour #evolution #recommended

docs.title: Noise — Daniel Kahneman, Olivier Sibony & Cass R. Sunstein
docs.text:
An examination of unwanted variability in human judgment, exploring why equally qualified people can reach very different decisions when considering the same evidence.

#decision-making #judgment #bias #psychology #statistics #organisations

docs.title: Determined — Robert M. Sapolsky
docs.text:
An exploration of human behaviour through biology, neuroscience, psychology, and environment, questioning conventional ideas about free will and individual responsibility.

#neuroscience #psychology #behaviour #biology #free-will #ethics

docs.title: Look Again — Tali Sharot & Cass R. Sunstein
docs.text:
An exploration of habituation and how becoming accustomed to our surroundings can make us overlook both problems and sources of pleasure, asking how changing perspective can help us notice them again.

#psychology #habituation #attention #perception #behaviour #perspective

docs.title: The Design of Everyday Things — Don Norman
docs.text:
An influential introduction to human-centred design, exploring how objects and systems communicate how they should be used and why poor design is often mistaken for user error.

#design #human-centred-design #usability #hci #psychology #problem-solving #recommended

docs.title: Photography & Society — Gisèle Freund
docs.text:
A social and historical examination of photography, exploring how photographic practices developed alongside changing technologies, social classes, political institutions, journalism, and mass culture.

#photography #visual-culture #history #society #media #representation

docs.title: A Short History of Photography — Walter Benjamin
docs.text:
An influential essay on the early history of photography, considering portraiture, technological change, reproduction, artistic value, and the changing ways photographs are made and encountered.

#photography #visual-culture #history #art #technology #critical-thinking

docs.title: The Work of Art in the Age of Mechanical Reproduction — Walter Benjamin
docs.text:
An influential essay examining how technologies of reproduction such as photography and film transform the status, circulation, experience, and political possibilities of art.

#photography #art #reproduction #technology #media #visual-culture #critical-thinking

docs.title: Camera Lucida — Roland Barthes
docs.text:
A personal and philosophical meditation on photography, memory, loss, attention, and the distinctive relationship between a photograph and the reality it records.

#photography #visual-culture #memory #representation #philosophy #art

docs.title: On Photography — Susan Sontag
docs.text:
A collection of essays examining photography as an artistic, social, and political practice, asking how photographs shape the ways we look at events, other people, suffering, and the world around us.

#photography #visual-culture #representation #ethics #media #society #critical-thinking #recommended

docs.title: Ways of Seeing — John Berger
docs.text:
An accessible and influential exploration of how we look at images, examining art, photography, advertising, gender, ownership, and the ways social and cultural contexts shape what we see.

#visual-culture #photography #art #advertising #representation #media-literacy #critical-thinking #recommended

docs.title: Another Way of Telling — John Berger & Jean Mohr
docs.text:
An exploration of how photographs create meaning and tell stories, combining photographic sequences and essays to investigate memory, narrative, context, and the relationship between images and words.

#photography #storytelling #visual-narrative #memory #representation #images-and-text #recommended

docs.title: Towards a Philosophy of Photography — Vilém Flusser
docs.text:
A philosophical examination of photography and photographic technology, asking how cameras shape the possibilities available to photographers and how technical images influence the ways we understand the world.

#photography #philosophy #technology #visual-culture #media #critical-thinking

docs.title: The Civil Contract of Photography — Ariella Aïsha Azoulay
docs.text:
A theoretical exploration of photography as a relationship between photographer, photographed person, and viewer, examining citizenship, power, violence, responsibility, and the politics of looking.

#photography #ethics #politics #representation #citizenship #power #visual-culture

docs.title: Listening to Images — Tina M. Campt
docs.text:
An exploration of archival photographs of Black communities and the quieter forms of expression, resistance, and possibility that can emerge when images are examined beyond their most immediately visible meanings.

#photography #archives #race #representation #history #visual-culture #critical-thinking

docs.title: Black Looks: Race and Representation — bell hooks
docs.text:
A collection of essays examining race, gender, representation, spectatorship, and the politics of looking across photography, film, television, and popular culture.

#visual-culture #race #gender #representation #media #critical-thinking

docs.title: Blind Spot — Teju Cole
docs.text:
A combination of photographs and short texts that explores travel, observation, memory, politics, coincidence, and the connections that emerge through attentive looking.

#photography #writing #observation #visual-storytelling #memory #place #art

docs.title: The Nature of Photographs — Stephen Shore
docs.text:
A concise introduction to understanding how photographs work as visual objects, examining framing, focus, time, viewpoint, composition, and the choices through which photographers transform the world into an image.

#photography #composition #visual-literacy #observation #art #practice

docs.title: The Photographer's Playbook: 307 Assignments and Ideas — Jason Fulford & Gregory Halpern (eds.)
docs.text:
A collection of assignments, exercises, ideas, and provocations from photographers and educators, designed to encourage experimentation, observation, creative risk-taking, and the development of an individual photographic practice.

#photography #practice #exercises #creativity #experimentation #observation #assignments #recommended

docs.title: Diane Arbus: An Aperture Monograph — Diane Arbus
docs.text:
An influential collection of Arbus's portraits, bringing together photographs of people, relationships, identities, and social worlds through a distinctive and sometimes unsettling approach to portraiture and observation.

#photography #portraiture #identity #representation #observation #society #visual-culture

docs.title: Photographs of Famous Men & Fair Women — Julia Margaret Cameron
docs.text:
A collection of portraits and staged photographs by one of the most distinctive photographers of the nineteenth century, offering a way to explore portraiture, expression, staging, focus, literary influence, and the emergence of photography as an artistic medium.

#photography #portraiture #history-of-photography #staging #women-photographers #visual-culture #art``#recommended

docs.title: Raised by Wolves — Jim Goldberg
docs.text:
A photographic and documentary work about young people living on the streets in California, combining photographs with handwritten texts, interviews, drawings, found materials, and other forms of testimony to construct a complex narrative between documentation and storytelling.

#photography #documentary #photobook #storytelling #text-and-image #youth #representation #recommended

docs.title: The Ballad of Sexual Dependency — Nan Goldin
docs.text:
An intensely personal photographic account of relationships, intimacy, friendship, sexuality, nightlife, love, conflict, and loss, constructed from photographs of Goldin herself and the communities around her.

#photography #photobook #intimacy #relationships #identity #community #diary #visual-narrative #recommended

docs.title: The Last Resort — Martin Parr
docs.text:
A vivid and often humorous photographic portrait of leisure and everyday life in the British seaside resort of New Brighton, using colour, observation, and visual irony to examine class, consumption, family life, and the ordinary.

#photography #documentary #colour #observation #everyday-life #consumer-culture #society #humour #recommended

docs.title: Utterly Lazy and Inattentive — Martin Parr
docs.text:
A retrospective selection of photographs chosen by Parr from across his career, bringing together decades of observation of everyday life, leisure, consumption, tourism, class, behaviour, and the absurdities of the ordinary.

#photography #documentary #observation #everyday-life #consumer-culture #humour #society #colour #recommended

docs.title: The Complete Untitled Film Stills — Cindy Sherman
docs.text:
A series of staged self-portraits in which Sherman performs fictional female characters reminiscent of film imagery, using photography to explore identity, gender, representation, stereotypes, and the construction of images.

#photography #self-portraiture #staging #gender #identity #representation #film #conceptual-art #recommended

docs.title: An American Exodus: A Record of Human Erosion — Dorothea Lange & Paul S. Taylor
docs.text:
A documentary study of migration, poverty, labour, and displacement during the Great Depression, combining Lange's photographs with Taylor's research, field notes, captions, and the words of the people they encountered.

#photography #documentary #migration #labour #poverty #history #text-and-image #social-documentary

docs.title: Narration in the Fiction Film — David Bordwell
docs.text:
An examination of how films communicate narrative information and how viewers construct stories through visual cues, editing, time, perspective, and cinematic conventions.

#film #narratology #cinema #visual-storytelling #cognition #editing #critical-thinking #recommended

docs.title: Actual Minds, Possible Worlds — Jerome Bruner
docs.text:
An exploration of different ways of constructing knowledge and meaning, examining the role of narrative in human thought, imagination, interpretation, and our understanding of experience.

#psychology #narrative #cognition #storytelling #meaning #imagination #recommended

docs.title: The Hero with a Thousand Faces — Joseph Campbell
docs.text:
An influential theory of recurring patterns in mythology and storytelling across different traditions. Campbell's idea of the 'monomyth' has had a major influence on modern storytelling, although its claim to universality has been challenged by scholars of mythology and folklore

#mythology #storytelling #narrative #culture

docs.title: Story and Discourse: Narrative Structure in Fiction and Film — Seymour Chatman
docs.text:
An exploration of narrative structure across literature and cinema, examining the distinction between story and discourse, narrative time, character, perspective, and the different ways stories are communicated through words and images.

#narratology #storytelling #literature #film #narrative-structure #representation #recommended

docs.title: Steering the Craft — Ursula K. Le Guin
docs.text:
A practical exploration of the craft of writing, focusing on language, rhythm, point of view, sentence construction, and narrative technique.

#writing #storytelling #creativity #craft

docs.title: On Writing — Stephen King
docs.text:
Part memoir and part practical guide to writing, reflecting on reading, discipline, revision, language, and the development of a writing practice.

#writing #storytelling #creativity #craft #recommended

docs.title: Understanding Comics: The Invisible Art — Scott McCloud 🆓
docs.text:
An accessible visual exploration of how sequential images communicate stories and ideas, examining framing, time, transitions, symbols, perception, and the relationship between images and words.

#visual-storytelling #comics #narrative #art #design #visual-literacy #creativity #recommended

docs.title: Orality and Literacy — Walter J. Ong
docs.text:
An influential examination of how oral and written forms of communication shape memory, expression, storytelling, and cultural practices, exploring the relationship between communication technologies and human thought.

#storytelling #oral-tradition #literacy #communication #media #culture #history

docs.title: Morphology of the Folktale — Vladimir Propp
docs.text:
A structural analysis of Russian folktales identifying recurring narrative functions and character roles, providing a foundational approach to studying patterns in storytelling.

#narratology #folklore #structuralism #storytelling #narrative-structure #literature #classic

docs.title: The Science of Storytelling — Will Storr
docs.text:
Here is one attempt to connect what we know about cognition with storytelling practice. It presents an exploration of storytelling through psychology and neuroscience, examining how character, change, curiosity, and models of the world shape narratives.

#storytelling #psychology #narrative #creativity

docs.title: Aristotle's Poetics for Screenwriters — Michael Tierno
docs.text: A practical interpretation of Aristotle's ideas about drama, adapted to the construction and analysis of contemporary screen stories. #storytelling #screenwriting #narrative #film #recommended

docs.title: The Anatomy of Story — John Truby 🆓
docs.text:
A practical framework for developing stories through character, motivation, moral choices, conflict, and interconnected narrative elements, offering an alternative to rigid act-based storytelling formulas.

#storytelling #screenwriting #character-development #narrative-structure #writing #creative-practice #recommended

docs.title: The Writer's Journey — Christopher Vogler
docs.text:
A practical story-design framework for storytelling based on recurring narrative patterns and the concept of the hero's journey.

#storytelling #narrative #screenwriting #structure

docs.title: Creativity, Inc. — Ed Catmull, with Amy Wallace
docs.text:
A reflection on creativity, collaboration, leadership, and organisational culture based on Catmull's experience building and leading Pixar.

#creativity #collaboration #leadership #organisations #creative-practice

docs.title: On Writing Well — William Zinsser
docs.text:
A practical guide to writing clear, concise, engaging non-fiction, with an emphasis on simplicity, revision, and respect for the reader.

#writing #communication #clarity #non-fiction

docs.title: Everybody Writes — Ann Handley
docs.text:
A practical guide to writing clearly and effectively for digital communication, from longer texts to everyday online content.

#writing #communication #digital-media #content

docs.title: Free Culture - Lawrence Lessig 🆓
docs.text:
An introduction to copyright, creativity, the public domain, and the impact of intellectual property law on innovation and culture.

#copyright #creative-commons #open-knowledge #digital-culture #intellectual-property #recommended

docs.title: Amusing Ourselves to Death — Neil Postman 🆓
docs.text:
A thought-provoking examination of how entertainment and mass media influence public discourse, education, and democratic life. Although written in 1985, many of its ideas resonate strongly in the age of social media.

#critical-thinking #media-literacy #education #communication #society #recommended

docs.title: The New Empire of AI — Rachel Adams
docs.text:
An examination of artificial intelligence through global inequality, exploring how AI systems depend on existing international distributions of labour, resources, wealth, and political power.

#ai #global-inequality #technology #power #labour #global-south #society

docs.title: On Internet Freedom — Marvin Ammori
docs.text:
An exploration of internet policy, freedom of expression, innovation, and the legal and political questions surrounding an open internet.

#internet #digital-rights #law #freedom-of-expression #technology #recommended

docs.title: Race After Technology — Ruha Benjamin
docs.text:
An examination of how technologies that appear neutral can reproduce and deepen racial inequality, introducing ways of thinking critically about the relationship between design, automation, classification, and discrimination.

#technology #race #algorithms #bias #design #inequality #society

docs.title: Dark Matters — Simone Browne
docs.text:
An exploration of surveillance through the history and experience of Black communities, connecting contemporary technologies such as biometrics and security systems with longer histories of racialised surveillance.

#surveillance #race #history #technology #biometrics #privacy #society

docs.title: Artificial Unintelligence — Meredith Broussard
docs.text:
A critique of the assumption that computers can or should solve every problem, exploring the limitations of computational systems and the consequences of treating technological solutions as inherently superior.

#ai #technology #algorithms #critical-thinking #technochauvinism #society

docs.title: More Than a Glitch — Meredith Broussard
docs.text:
An examination of how racism, sexism, and ableism can become embedded in technological systems, arguing that discriminatory outcomes should not simply be treated as isolated technical errors.

#ai #algorithms #bias #race #gender #disability #inequality #technology

docs.title: Unmasking AI — Joy Buolamwini
docs.text:
A personal and research-informed account of uncovering bias in facial-analysis technologies and the wider effort to challenge discrimination and exclusion in artificial intelligence.

#ai #facial-recognition #algorithms #bias #race #gender #accountability

docs.title: Brotopia — Emily Chang
docs.text:
An investigation into gender inequality and workplace culture in Silicon Valley, examining how the technology industry's institutions, networks, and working environments have shaped who participates in building technology and who holds power within the industry.

#technology #silicon-valley #gender #women-in-technology #workplace-culture #inequality #EDI

docs.title: Atlas of AI — Kate Crawford
docs.text:
An examination of artificial intelligence as a material and political system, considering data, labour, natural resources, classification, and power alongside the technology itself.

#ai #technology #data #labour #power #ethics #society #recommended

docs.title: The AI Con — Emily M. Bender & Alex Hanna
docs.text:
A critical examination of claims made about artificial intelligence, asking what current AI systems actually do, who benefits from exaggerated expectations about them, and what social and material costs can be obscured by the language surrounding AI. It's a deliberately sceptical examination of contemporary AI claims and industry narratives. Best read alongside technically grounded accounts offering different assessments of AI capabilities and limitations.

#ai #critical-thinking #technology #language-models #industry #labour #power

docs.title: Empire of AI — Karen Hao
docs.text:
A reported investigation into the development of the contemporary AI industry, examining its institutions, ambitions, labour, environmental resources, and concentrations of power through the history and expansion of OpenAI.

#ai #technology #labour #environment #power #industry #society

docs.title: Your Face Belongs to Us — Kashmir Hill
docs.text:
An investigation into the development of Clearview AI and the rapid expansion of facial-recognition technology, examining privacy, surveillance, data collection, law enforcement, and the consequences of making faces searchable at scale.

#facial-recognition #privacy #surveillance #ai #biometrics #data #digital-rights

docs.title: AI Snake Oil — Arvind Narayanan & Sayash Kapoor
docs.text:
An evidence-based examination of what artificial intelligence can and cannot reliably do, distinguishing genuine advances from exaggerated claims and investigating areas such as predictive algorithms, generative AI, automated decision-making, and the AI industry.

#ai #critical-thinking #evidence #algorithms #prediction #generative-ai #technology

docs.title: Silicon Valley Imperialism — Erin McElroy
docs.text:
An examination of how Silicon Valley's models of technology, investment, property, and development travel across borders, connecting the San Francisco Bay Area with postsocialist Romania through questions of displacement, inequality, and technological power.

#technology #silicon-valley #globalisation #inequality #housing #political-economy #europe

docs.title: Blood in the Machine — Brian Merchant
docs.text:
A history of the Luddites and their resistance to the ways industrial technologies were being used to transform labour, wages, skills, and power during the Industrial Revolution, connecting their experience with contemporary debates about automation.

#technology #labour #history #automation #industrial-revolution #workers #society

docs.title: Dying for an iPhone — Jenny Chan, Mark Selden & Pun Ngai
docs.text:
An investigation into the human labour behind global electronics manufacturing, examining factory conditions, worker experiences, supply chains, and the social costs embedded in consumer technology.

#technology #labour #china #supply-chains #manufacturing #globalisation #inequality

docs.title: Obfuscation — Finn Brunton & Helen Nissenbaum
docs.text:
An exploration of techniques for resisting pervasive data collection by deliberately producing ambiguous or misleading information, combining practical examples with questions about privacy, power, protest, and the ethics of resisting surveillance.

#privacy #surveillance #data #digital-rights #resistance #ethics #technology

docs.title: Algorithms of Oppression — Safiya Umoja Noble
docs.text:
An examination of how search engines can reproduce and amplify racism and sexism, challenging the assumption that information technologies and their results are inherently neutral.

#algorithms #search-engines #race #gender #bias #technology #inequality

docs.title: Weapons of Math Destruction — Cathy O'Neil
docs.text:
An accessible examination of how mathematical models and algorithmic decision systems can reproduce inequality when they are opaque, difficult to challenge, and applied at scale in areas such as education, employment, credit, and criminal justice.

#algorithms #data #bias #inequality #accountability #critical-thinking #recommended

docs.title: Against Tech Oligarchy — J. S. Tan & Clarissa Redwine
docs.text:
An account of worker organising within the technology industry, examining employee protests, unionisation, workplace conflict, corporate power, and changing relationships between technology workers and the companies they help build.

#technology #labour #workers #unions #silicon-valley #corporate-power #society

docs.title: The Mechanic and the Luddite — Jathan Sadowski
docs.text:
A critical examination of the relationship between technology and economic systems, asking how technologies are designed, deployed, owned, and used and arguing for evaluating technological change in relation to its social and material consequences.

#technology #capitalism #labour #data #political-economy #critical-thinking #society

docs.title: The Algorithm — Hilke Schellmann
docs.text:
An investigative examination of algorithmic systems used in hiring, workplace monitoring, promotion, and employment decisions, including real-world tests of tools that claim to evaluate workers and job candidates.

#ai #algorithms #work #employment #bias #surveillance #accountability

docs.title: Ghost Work — Mary L. Gray & Siddharth Suri
docs.text:
An investigation into the often invisible human labour behind digital platforms and artificial intelligence, examining the people who label, moderate, verify, and otherwise perform tasks that automated systems cannot complete alone.

#ai #labour #platforms #automation #gig-economy #technology #society #recommended

docs.title: The AI Mirror — Shannon Vallor
docs.text:
An examination of what artificial intelligence reflects about human values, assumptions, and institutions, and how thinking about AI can become a way of thinking about ourselves.

#ai #ethics #technology #philosophy #society #recommended

docs.title: Prophecy — Carissa Véliz
docs.text:
An examination of the human desire to predict the future and the growing use of data and artificial intelligence to forecast behaviour, questioning the power acquired by institutions that claim to anticipate what people will do.

#ai #prediction #data #privacy #power #technology #philosophy

docs.title: Careless People — Sarah Wynn-Williams
docs.text:
A first-person account of working inside Facebook during its transformation into one of the world's most influential technology companies, exploring corporate culture, leadership, global expansion, platform power, and the consequences of decisions made behind technologies used by billions of people.

#social-media #facebook #instagram #technology #platforms #corporate-culture #power #digital-society

docs.title: The Age of Surveillance Capitalism — Shoshana Zuboff
docs.text:
An extensive examination of the collection and commercial use of behavioural data and the economic systems that have developed around digital surveillance.

#privacy #surveillance #technology #data #economics #society #recommended

docs.title: Fix the System, Not the Women — Laura Bates
docs.text:
An examination of structural gender inequality across education, work, politics, media, and everyday life, arguing that persistent inequalities require attention to systems rather than asking individual women to adapt to them.

#gender-equality #women #discrimination #work #society #EDI #recommended

docs.title: Invisible Women — Caroline Criado Perez
docs.text:
An examination of gender data gaps and the ways apparently neutral decisions in areas such as medicine, transport, technology, and public policy can produce unequal outcomes.

#gender #data #design #bias #women #inequality #EDI #recommended

docs.title: The Authority Gap — Mary Ann Sieghart
docs.text:
An exploration of persistent differences in how women's expertise and authority are perceived, heard, and valued in professional and public life.

#gender #authority #bias #work #women #EDI

docs.title: About this collection
docs.text:
Welcome! This repository is an evolving curated collection of books, articles, papers, videos, courses, websites, you name it! It offers selected starting points for exploring new ideas. Curiosity, critical thinking and independent learning are essential skills for every student. I hope these support you in your quests, lead you somewhere unexpected, and allow you to have fun along the way.

Resources are organised by topic and, whenever possible, include: - a short description; - why the resource is valuable; - the expected level of difficulty; - recommended prerequisites.

This repository intends to be a living collection maintained by the community. Everyone is encouraged to contribute by suggesting new resources, improving descriptions or correcting outdated information.

docs.title: Guiding principles
docs.text:
• Be curious;
  • Think critically;
  • Verify your sources;
  • Learn continuously;
  • Share what you discover.

docs.title: Code of conduct
docs.text: This repository is part of an extensive learning community. Everyone should feel welcome to learn, ask questions and share knowledge. If anything triggers you, feel free to reach out to me.

docs.title: Expectations
docs.text: You are encouraged to: - Treat others with respect. - Be curious and open-minded. - Support claims with reliable evidence. - Give constructive feedback. - Acknowledge mistakes and learn from them. - Credit the work of others.

docs.title: Unacceptable behaviour
docs.text: This includes, but is not limited to: - Harassment or discrimination; - Personal attacks; - Plagiarism; - Deliberate misinformation; - Disruptive or disrespectful behaviour.

docs.title: Philosophy
docs.text: Learning is collaborative. Nobody knows everything, and everyone has something to contribute. - Be curious; - Be brave; - Be kind; - Keep learning.

docs.title: Repository structure
docs.text:
The collection is organised by type of resource, with topics and themes connecting materials across sections. It is a work in progress (wip) which will evolve into something like: - Readings - Fiction - Non-Fiction - In the Media (wip) - Scientific Papers (wip) - Glossary - Courses (wip) - Multimedia (wip) - Tools (wip)

Happy exploring!

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: Thank you for helping improve this repository, and build a collection of high-quality learning resources that benefits everyone in the community.

docs.title: Before adding a resource
docs.text: Ask yourself: - Is it accurate and trustworthy? - Does it add something that isn't already here? - Is it appropriate for the intended audience? - Have you read or watched it yourself?

docs.title: Adding a resource
docs.text: Whenever possible, include: - Title - Author - Link - Topic - Difficulty (Beginner / Intermediate / Advanced) - Why it's worth exploring (2–3 sentences)

docs.title: Improving existing resources
docs.text: Contributions don't have to be new ideas. You can also: - fix mistakes; - improve descriptions; - update broken links; - suggest better alternatives; - reorganise content.

docs.title: Be respectful
docs.text:
Different perspectives are welcome, but discussions should remain respectful, evidence-based and constructive.

Every contribution is an opportunity to help someone else learn.

docs.title: Glossary · Think like you care
docs.text:
This glossary accompanies the Think Like You Care module. It's not something to memorise, but a resource to explore and return to whenever a word or concept trips you up. Each entry includes a short definition, an example, links to related terms, and the Portuguese equivalent used in the module slides. Suggestions and contributions are always welcome.

Jump to: A · B · C · D · E · F · G · H · I · L · M · O · P · R · S

docs.title: Ad hominem
docs.text: A fallacy that attacks the person instead of answering their argument. - Example: "Don't listen to what he says about the climate: he didn't even finish secondary school." - See also: Fallacy - PT: ad hominem

docs.title: AI hallucination
docs.text: When an AI tool makes up information (a figure, a quote, a source) and presents it with total confidence, as if it were true. - Example: A chatbot recommends a book whose title and author don't exist. - See also: Generative AI - PT: alucinação (IA)

docs.title: Algorithm
docs.text: A set of rules a program follows to make a decision. On social media, the algorithm chooses what appears in your feed, usually based on what keeps you on the screen. - Example: You watched three cooking videos and now your feed is full of them. - See also: Filter bubble, Attention economy - PT: algoritmo

docs.title: Argument
docs.text: A set of reasons (premises) that support an idea (a conclusion). - Example: "Not sleeping enough hurts concentration. I have a test tomorrow. So I should go to bed early." - See also: Premise, Conclusion, Evidence - PT: argumento

docs.title: Attention economy
docs.text: A business model where your attention is the product: the longer you spend on an app, the more money it makes from advertising. That's why content that triggers strong emotions (outrage, fear, surprise) tends to get promoted more. - See also: Algorithm, Emotional reasoning - PT: economia da atenção

docs.title: Bandwagon effect
docs.text: The tendency to believe or do something because lots of other people do. - Example: "Everyone in class already has this app, so it must be safe." - See also: Cognitive bias - PT: efeito de manada

docs.title: Barnum effect
docs.text: The tendency to accept vague descriptions that could fit anyone as if they were "made for us". Also called the Forer effect. - Example: A horoscope says "sometimes you're sociable, other times you'd rather be alone", and it feels like it knows you. - See also: Cognitive bias - PT: efeito Barnum

docs.title: Cognitive bias
docs.text: A mental shortcut that distorts our reasoning without us noticing. Everyone has them: the goal isn't to pretend they don't exist, but to learn to recognise them. - Examples: confirmation bias, bandwagon effect, emotional reasoning, Barnum effect. - PT: viés cognitivo

docs.title: Conclusion
docs.text: The idea an argument is trying to support. - Example: In "It's raining, so I'll take an umbrella", the conclusion is "I'll take an umbrella". - PT: conclusão

docs.title: Confirmation bias
docs.text: The tendency to look for, notice and remember mainly the information that confirms what we already think. - Example: We only follow people who think like us and ignore everyone else. - Tip: Ask yourself: "What would make me change my mind?" - See also: Hypothesis, Filter bubble - PT: viés de confirmação

docs.title: CRAAP test
docs.text:
Five questions for evaluating a source:

Letter Criterion Question PT C Currency When was it published? Is it still up to date? Atualidade R Relevance Does it actually answer my question? Relevância A Authority Who wrote it? Do they know the subject? Autoridade A Accuracy Is there evidence? Do other sources confirm it? Precisão P Purpose Is it trying to inform, sell, persuade or entertain? Propósito
  • See also: Source, Credibility
  • PT: teste CRAAP

docs.title: Credibility
docs.text: How much trust a source deserves. It depends on who's writing, what they know about the subject, the evidence they give and their intentions. - Example: An article by a medical specialist, citing studies, has more credibility on health than an anonymous comment. - PT: credibilidade

docs.title: Critical thinking
docs.text: Analysing information carefully to reach a well-founded judgement. It isn't having the right answer to everything, or being contrary: it's wanting to be well informed, enjoying putting ideas to the test, and being open to changing your mind. - PT: pensamento crítico

docs.title: Deepfake
docs.text: A fake video, image or audio clip made with AI that looks real. It can make someone appear to say or do something they never said or did. - Example: A video of a public figure announcing something they never announced. - See also: Reverse image search - PT: deepfake

docs.title: Disinformation
docs.text: False or misleading information created on purpose to deceive, whether to make money, sway opinions or cause confusion. - Example: A website invents a shocking story to generate clicks and advertising revenue. - See also: Misinformation - PT: desinformação

docs.title: Echo chamber
docs.text: A space (online or offline) where we only hear opinions like our own, repeated and reinforced. The difference from a filter bubble: the bubble is created by the algorithm; the echo chamber is created by us, when we only follow people who think like us. - Example: A group chat where everyone always agrees, and anyone who disagrees ends up leaving. - PT: câmara de eco

docs.title: Emotional reasoning
docs.text: Believing something is true because we feel it's true. - Example: A video that makes us angry instantly seems believable. - Tip: When something makes you angry or afraid, that's the moment to slow down, not to share. - See also: Cognitive bias - PT: raciocínio emocional

docs.title: Evidence
docs.text: Facts, data or proof that support, or challenge, an idea. - Example: A study with thousands of participants is stronger evidence than a single personal story. - See also: Argument, Fact - PT: evidência

docs.title: Fact
docs.text: Something that can be checked: measured, observed, confirmed by independent sources. - Example: "This app has 50 million users." - See also: Interpretation, Opinion - PT: facto

docs.title: Fact-checking
docs.text: Journalistic work that checks whether a claim is true, misleading or false. In Portugal: Polígrafo and Observador Fact Check. - See also: Lateral reading - PT: verificação de factos

docs.title: Fallacy
docs.text: A reasoning error that makes an argument look good when it isn't. There are many; three of the most common are ad hominem, the straw man and the false dilemma. - See also: Argument - PT: falácia

docs.title: False dilemma
docs.text: A fallacy that presents only two options, usually extreme ones, as if there were no others. - Example: "Either you quit social media, or you'll be addicted forever." - See also: Fallacy - PT: falso dilema

docs.title: Filter bubble
docs.text: When algorithms mostly show you content similar to what you already think or like, and you stop seeing other perspectives. - Example: Two people search for the same news story and get very different results. - See also: Echo chamber, Algorithm - PT: bolha de filtro

docs.title: Generative AI
docs.text: Artificial intelligence that can create new content (text, images, audio, video) from instructions. It's a useful tool, but its answers need checking too. - Example: Conversational chatbots and image generators. - See also: AI hallucination, Deepfake - PT: IA generativa

docs.title: Hypothesis
docs.text: A provisional explanation or idea that still needs testing. A good thinker also looks for the evidence that could prove it wrong. - Example: In the 2-4-6 challenge, "even numbers going up by 2" is a hypothesis, and it's wrong! - See also: Confirmation bias - PT: hipótese

docs.title: Inference
docs.text: A conclusion we reach from clues or evidence. - Example: The ground is wet and people are carrying umbrellas: you infer that it rained. - See also: Conclusion - PT: inferência

docs.title: Interpretation
docs.text: One possible reading of the facts. Two well-informed people can interpret the same facts differently, and that's legitimate. - Example: "The app is successful because it's very addictive." (Someone else might say: "…because it's really useful.") - See also: Fact, Opinion - PT: interpretação

docs.title: Lateral reading
docs.text: A technique used by professional fact-checkers: instead of spending a long time on a website trying to work out whether it's reliable, you open other tabs and see what other sources say about it. - See also: Fact-checking, Source - PT: leitura lateral

docs.title: Misinformation
docs.text: False information shared without intending to deceive, for example by someone who believed it. - Example: A relative forwards a fake "health tip" because they think they're helping. - See also: Disinformation - PT: informação errada

docs.title: Opinion
docs.text: What someone thinks or values about a subject. It can't be proven like a fact, but it can (and should) be backed by good arguments. - Example: "Young people should spend less time on social media." - See also: Fact, Interpretation - PT: opinião

docs.title: Premise
docs.text: A statement used as a reason or starting point in an argument. An argument is only strong if the logic works and the premises are true. - Example: "Videos with millions of views are usually true." (This premise is false!) - PT: premissa

docs.title: Reverse image search
docs.text: Searching with an image (instead of words) to find out where it has appeared before and in what context. Tools: Google Lens, TinEye. - Example: You discover that the photo "from yesterday" has actually been circulating since 2015. - See also: Deepfake - PT: pesquisa inversa de imagens

docs.title: Source
docs.text: Where a piece of information comes from: who produced it and where it was published. - See also: Credibility, CRAAP test, Lateral reading - PT: fonte

docs.title: Sponsored content
docs.text: Content paid for by a brand, which can look like a personal opinion or a news story. By law it should be labelled (#ad, "paid partnership"). - Example: An influencer praises a supplement the brand gave them for free. - See also: CRAAP test (Purpose) - PT: conteúdo patrocinado

docs.title: Straw man
docs.text:
A fallacy that distorts or exaggerates what someone said, to make it easier to attack. - Example: "You want to ban phones in class? So you want to go back to the Stone Age!" - See also: Fallacy - PT: espantalho

Missing a word? This glossary is updated with current topics. Suggest new terms to the workshop facilitator.

Last updated: October 2026.
